request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: 25-year-old female
Admission date: [DATE]
Discharge date: [DATE]
Length of stay: [NUMBER] days
Admission Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient presented to the emergency department with complaints of acute onset of epigastric pain and nausea with bilious emesis. Initial workup did not demonstrate evidence of biliary or gallbladder pathology. However, her symptoms progressed and she was re-evaluated with a computed tomography that demonstrated a soft tissue mass located posterior to the gallbladder. Further evaluation with magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography observed a complex cystic structure of indeterminate etiology at the porta hepatis.

The patient underwent surgery, during which a hemorrhagic pedunculated mass attached to the infundibulum of the gallbladder was identified and resected. A cholecystectomy was also performed due to inflammation from the hemorrhagic mass. Gross pathology and histology revealed a hemorrhagic benign ectopic liver tissue, and localized cholecystitis in the area adjacent to the mass was also observed.

The patient's postoperative course was uneventful and her symptoms resolved immediately. She was discharged home on the first postoperative day and was asymptomatic when seen in follow-up.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:
The patient underwent surgery to remove the hemorrhagic benign ectopic liver tissue and cholecystitis. She was discharged with instructions to follow up with her healthcare provider.

Condition at Discharge:
The patient was asymptomatic and in stable condition at the time of discharge.

Discharge Medications: N/A

Follow-up:
The patient was instructed to follow up with her healthcare provider.

Instructions:
The patient was instructed to follow up with her healthcare provider.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for this admission is the haemorrhagic ectopic (accessory) liver tissue attached to the gallbladder.

1. **What was found.** The symptomatic lesion was a haemorrhagic, pedunculated mass on the gallbladder infundibulum. Histology showed it was benign ectopic liver tissue.
2. **Why it is the principal diagnosis.** Haemorrhage into this tissue caused the epigastric pain and vomiting, and resecting it was the main reason for surgery. The localised cholecystitis was secondary inflammation next to the mass, so it is an additional diagnosis rather than the principal one.
3. **Chapter Q.** Ectopic or accessory liver tissue is a developmental anomaly. It is therefore classified with congenital malformations, not with neoplasms (D) or digestive diseases (K).
4. **Category 44.** Q44 covers congenital malformations of the gallbladder, bile ducts and liver. Accessory liver falls under Q44.7, other congenital malformations of liver.

CODE: Q44
